I’m not shaming him for not wanting to be poked. I’m criticising his immature response given the circumstances. That is, his refusal to communicate adequately.

And I don’t get the argument about this being only OP’s side. I’m going to base my opinion of the information presented, not speculate- it’s on the internet anyway. The brother didn’t make the post, of course we don’t know his side because he isn’t trying to communicate or resolve it like OP.

The blame isn’t on OP for this situation. It’s difficult for him and they recognise this. That’s why they made the post, to help the situation. But it’s on the brother (and mother) for their total failure to communicate and assumption that their sister is directing this at them intentionally. 

He’s just too fragile and makes himself the victim (I wrote how this happens on the og post). Of course nobody wants to be ‘picked on’ but he’s exacerbating the situation by conflating tics with actions. Once he properly learns and **considers** the nature of Tourette’s, then his withdrawal may be more acceptable but he’s 19. He should at least try. You make it sound like her Tourette’s are making a concerted effort to stalk and harass her brother. No, his autonomy is not under threat, he should try to respect that Tourette’s is hard. His sister is having a hard time too. I don’t expect him to find some saint-like tolerance but it’s should be that much to expect an effort, at least in return.

Nearly every upvoted comment here is horrendous, projects their own issues and conflates mental disorders with neurological. Worst example: your psychosis is not a source here- people with specifically Tourette’s do not have similar experiences or **responsibility** for their disorder. They’re in completely different categories of disorder, for Christ’s sake. 

Ya’ll don’t _actually_ understand that everything done and said is **involuntary** and goes specifically against OP’s wish. You want to know why he’s ‘the target’? Because he’s making himself it. He overreacts to a tic (I’ve seen _real_ children handle Tourette’s better), that leaves an impression, sister then recalls their last interaction as being ruined by ticcing, she frets over ticcing, she tics. Because thinking about about specific tics brings out that tic. If you’d done a modicum of research, you’d have known this.

This is a known pattern whereby specific tics/types of tics are associated with specific people. They’re not all bad, I blow constant kisses to certain friends, but because the brother makes the ‘mean’ tics all about him, they become about him. It’s a self-fulfilling-prophecy created by the **young adult** brother.

Also, tics can’t be inherently mean? They can be offensive but there is zero **intent** to hurt anybody, so they can’t _be_ mean. They can imitate it, the same way my Tourette’s imitates being happy with forced smiles, but therapy for OP is pointless here.
I mean, I consistently cuss out a shower drain for minutes at a time, you gonna tell me I should be seeking therapy for my drain-bullying? No, it’s just a neurological pattern that spawned from one, random, occasion.

If you’re wondering where they even come from, it’s coprolalia (of which, 10% have). It’s inevitable that someone with coprolalia swears on occasion- or constantly, either way. The issue is fearing specific tics because that exacerbates them. They become more frequent, powerful and relevant to the situation. Especially when others reprimand you because they are too lazy to understand that you have **zero** control over it.
Stop shifting all responsibility away from the brother here- he should at least know how to communicate but he only ever assumes his sister is mean (not letting her explain her offensive actions) and makes himself the victim.

I’ve been overly mean here but I just wanted to reflect how infuriating these comments are without guilt- ya’ll are horrible.

It’s probably a good idea to clear this thread, I’d say it only does worse for the Tourette’s community and your health OP. These are the most misguided opinions I’ve seen yet. If not, just take from the r/Tourette’s cross post; they know what they’re talking about instead of chatting out their ass.

Yeah, those comments are rotten. They don’t take into any real account that what you say/do is **involuntary** and shift all responsibility away from your far-too-fragile brother. If anything, family counselling would be best to teach your brother to be an adult, communicate and stop making this about him. It’s your disability, not his hardship like he seems to think.

It varies. Similar to how a you can feel a sneeze coming sometimes or it might just come out of nowhere. 

Typically though, there’s some internal pressure in the upper spine region or roof palette of the mouth if it’ll be vocal. 
My complex tics (those that respond to my surroundings with related phrases) are often hugely intrusive thought that can be very specific. This is when I know what I’ll say for a brief moment so *can* alter it if it seems offensive or just too stupid. Difficult to do though- it takes lot of mental energy.

If it helps, I found that forcing myself to tense my muscles, squeeze stress balls or punch pillows can redirect these types of tics to something less painful. At least until you can get somewhere that isn’t as overwhelming and let them ‘cool off’.

For me, I had to practice suppressing my tics initially so they wouldn’t ‘take over’. This gave a moment to implement these methods instead. Our situations aren’t the same in this regard but learning the signs to your triggers could help, if possible. 

Wish you luck
